## Historical audit — S0334

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_v3/results/H04/test/bw_0011/2/trajectory.jsonl`. Citations below refer to its JSONL lines. The supplied observations contain no split lines.

| Stage | Evidence and limits |
|---|---|
| Goal | The task was to reconstruct one indoor photograph as editable SceneAct/Blender geometry, matching camera and appearance without using the reference as a texture. H’s inventory interpreted it as blue walls, cabinet, dandelion mural, display, floor and exposed ceiling; these semantic identifications are H’s estimates, not independently inspected images (lines 1, 3). |
| First build | H emitted multiple named assets and children: wall seams and coves, cabinet frames, shelves, doors and handles, geometric mural filaments, display and ceiling parts. Code used colors, opacity and lighting, but no reference texture. Hierarchy demonstrates emitted parts, not physical connection or image completeness; no articulated subject pose is evident (lines 3–4). |
| Feedback and revision | Step 1 built and rendered successfully (lines 6, 8–9). H reported a small isolated room, hidden clock and faint cabinet/mural, then moved the camera, extended floor/ceiling and revised local geometry and colors. These are H’s visual assessments, not independent verification (lines 11, 13–14). Step 2 also built and rendered successfully (lines 16, 18–19). |
| Final changes | H reported the right cove cropped and surfaces washed out; it shortened the right wall, retained the camera, shifted/widened the mural, adjusted the cabinet, darkened materials and reduced lighting. The complete program was executed, not merely proposed (lines 23–24). Step 3 built and rendered successfully and was selected (lines 26, 28–30). |
| Validation | Numerical projections compared estimated reference anchors with computed points. In step 3, the cove endpoint was computed at (0.876, 0.983) versus estimated (0.91, 0.91); a trial upward aim was restored. These are point checks, not visibility or surface verification (lines 23, 29). The final render is recorded, but no subsequent visual review is visible. |
| Input and exploration | The task and runner supplied instructions, reference and rendered images, and comparison prompts actually present in H’s requests (lines 1, 11, 21). No separate teacher diagnosis or teacher-proposed patch is visible; adoption of such advice cannot be claimed. H independently selected revisions and tested aim within its programs. Its sessions recorded no interactive tool calls (lines 2, 12, 22). |

**Outcome:** Technical execution succeeded for all three builds; step 3 was selected. **Visual/geometric correctness remains unknown**, not formal success or a demonstrated algorithm failure. There is no empty patch or technical interruption in the visible record. Names, projections and successful renders do not verify textures, occlusions, part contacts, framing or lighting against the unseen images.

**Lessons and uncertainty:** Separating camera landmarks from local asset parameters and checking trial directions is transferable, but does not replace image comparison. The shortened wall and darker mural are task-specific hypotheses; whether they improved the final image remains unresolved. The audit cannot determine final object completeness, material fidelity, connections or lighting quality from the supplied text alone.
